Reconstruct the visible indoor scene from one RGB photograph using SceneAct and Blender.
Infer geometry and a camera matching the reference viewpoint, perspective and framing.
Use separate 3D meshes for architecture, furniture and visible objects, preserving colors,
proportions, placement, occlusions and materials. Do not use the reference as a texture,
background or projected image. No ground-truth calibration or other views are available.

Return a complete, runnable Python program inside one ```python code block. Each execution
starts in a fresh Blender process. Programs can use numpy, sceneact and bpy. Use SceneAct
for geometry and relationships; bpy may customize lighting, materials and camera settings.
Do not render or save files in the program: the fixed runner saves and renders once after
execution, using your active camera. Do not access external files, network or other models.
When satisfied after inspecting a rendering, reply exactly DONE. The last successful build
is submitted automatically. Budget includes all planning, corrections and review calls.

Reference inventory and parameterization:
Before building, record a short reference inventory in program comments: major visible
objects, approximate normalized image bounds, distinctive visible parts, overlaps, and
uncertain or occluded regions. These are estimates from the current input, not calibration.
Map each inventory item to a named SceneAct asset with meaningful child parts. A valid
hierarchy verifies only the parts emitted; it does not establish photographic completeness.
Do not invent hidden details to fill uncertainty or omit visible parts because they are small.
Keep each object's local dimensions and shape parameters separate from its placement,
orientation and instance scale. Construct reusable assets in a consistent local frame, then
place their grouped subtrees with explicit pivots. Preserve independent editable instances,
semantic child parts and support relations. Keep camera parameters separate from geometry.

Local shape, projected size and depth:
For each visually important composite, estimate its overall contour, component proportions,
occupied space and gaps before adding fine repeated detail. Record a few visible landmarks
or contour ratios inside its estimated image bounds, such as transitions in width, attachment
points, rim position, opening shape and the visible interior fraction. Choose landmarks
supported by the image; do not require uncertain or occluded boundaries to be measurable.
A matching bounding box does not establish a matching profile, internal density or opening.

Treat local profile, overall scale, depth, orientation and camera as distinct parameter
families. Uniform scaling cannot repair an incorrect part-to-whole ratio. Moving an object
along a camera ray changes its projected size and may resemble scaling; one image usually
does not resolve that ambiguity. Use neighboring overlaps, support relationships, repeated
instances and perspective anchors as additional constraints, without claiming unique depth.
If bounding placement is reasonable but the contour or internal ratios differ, first consider
local profile parameters. If contour ratios agree but the footprint differs, consider scale
and depth together with support and occlusion evidence. Inspect orientation before changing
geometry when an opening or thin surface has the wrong apparent aspect or exposure.

Represent a clearly visible cavity or opening with geometry that admits the required view
of its inner surface. A flat cap is appropriate only when it explains the observed appearance;
it cannot generally substitute for a recessed interior or open shell. Keep outer profile,
rim thickness, opening dimensions and interior depth independently adjustable when visible.
Use a small number of supported solids and Boolean operations. Avoid coincident surfaces,
accidental filled openings and decorative complexity that does not affect the visible shape.
Do not automatically add hollowness to objects whose interiors are not evidenced.

Camera and local geometry remain competing explanations. Compare multiple independent
anchors spanning the image and depth range: major boundary lines, object centers, relative
sizes and overlap order. Shared projection discrepancies justify considering a camera change;
a local contour discrepancy justifies considering local shape. Neither pattern proves a cause.
Focal length primarily changes magnification; camera rotation changes framing and projected
orientation; camera position changes viewing direction relative to objects and parallax.
Rotation alone does not reproduce a different viewpoint into a cavity. Do not compensate
for every local mismatch by changing the camera or for every shared mismatch by moving objects.
Repeated objects provide useful consistency constraints, but their apparent differences may
come from perspective, occlusion, orientation or real variation; do not force equal image sizes.

Execution and review procedure:
Use the first execution for a compact complete scene, leaving the second available for
correction. Before execution, check inventory coverage, hierarchy, major projected placement,
contours, support and intended openings as far as the available evidence permits.
After a successful render, compare it with the original reference at two scales. First inspect
framing, major bright and dark regions, perspective anchors, relative sizes and overlap order.
Then inspect the contours, interior exposure, component proportions and gaps of prominent
objects. Distinguish geometry evidence from illumination, material and render-noise effects.
Do not use a global material override to conceal unresolved geometry or projection errors.

In comments of a revision, list a few largest supported discrepancies, the evidence for each,
and the parameter family being changed. Prefer the smallest coherent revision supported by
that evidence. Preserve already matching assets and their group structure. When multiple
families must change within the available budget, report the revision as a combined correction,
not a causal experiment. Recheck shared anchors after local changes and local contours after
camera changes. Keep unresolved correspondences and occluded geometry explicitly uncertain.
Do not impose one fixed camera, density, object count or correction across different inputs.

If intervention observations are supplied, distinguish measured outcomes from forecasts and
from a module-selection decision. Interpret each measured intervention under its actual
baseline, fixed parameters and score definition. A positive similarity change demonstrates
appearance sensitivity, not geometry truth or unique causation. Overlapping or absent outcomes
leave competing explanations unresolved. Do not invent probe results or request tools outside
the Runtime API. An isolated-object view can clarify membership and silhouette; its full-image
score does not establish that removing the rest of the scene improves reconstruction.
Mechanical checks and emitted-part integrity do not establish semantic completeness, true
support or collision correctness. Approximate projected AABBs are localization aids; boxes
crossing the camera plane can have extreme projected extents and require clipping or rendered
inspection before interpretation. Do not move or delete a group solely because of such bounds.

Execution cost planning:
The entire solve has three model calls, two Blender executions and 600 seconds. Use the
reported remaining budget when deciding whether another build and review are possible.
A short Python loop can generate thousands of Blender objects before any image exists.
Plan a compact complete first build so realization and the runner's render leave time for
review. Do not change the runner's resource policy or rendering settings to evade this budget.
Use geometry complexity as the controllable cost.
Before returning code, estimate expanded primitive counts in comments, including nested
loops and helper calls. Each ball, rod and box emits a separate mesh and marker; fillet_box
can expand to 26 primitives; sweep_tube with n points emits 2*n-1 primitives. Cloning and
layout helpers duplicate contents. Boolean operands incur mesh creation and modifier work.
Count these expansions, not just named assets. Aim initially for a few hundred primitive
meshes across the scene as a planning heuristic, not a runtime guarantee or fixed limit.
Allocate geometry according to visible pixel size, contour, openings, gaps and occlusion.
Prioritize a few adjustable shape-defining parts over dense decoration on an inaccurate form.
If estimates reach thousands, simplify repeated microstructure while retaining inventory
coverage and meaningful editable parts. Use shared materials and restrained procedural shading
for unresolved surface detail, retaining geometry that changes contours or occlusions.
Use short, adaptively spaced tube paths, concentrating points at bends. Avoid many nearly
identical Boolean slices for one hollow shape. Prefer boxes or scaled balls where their
silhouettes suffice; reserve fillet_box for visibly important rounded edges. Use a small
reusable material palette rather than a separate random material for every tiny primitive.
Do not flatten the hierarchy or merge semantic objects to reduce complexity.
If execution times out without an image, completion failed and the bottleneck is unknown
unless logs locate it. If a retry remains, reduce expanded primitives, Boolean operations
and material proliferation in the complete program. Do not infer camera, coverage or appearance
defects from a timeout. A cheaper build still requires execution and rendered verification;
simplification alone is not evidence of success.

Execution verification:
realize(scene) clears Blender to an empty factory scene. Configure the world, camera,
lighting and materials after realization; do not assume a default world exists. When setting
world nodes, use this initialization after realize:
    sc = bpy.context.scene
    if sc.world is None:
        sc.world = bpy.data.worlds.new('SceneWorld')
    sc.world.use_nodes = True
    background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('Background')
    if background is None:
        background = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeBackground')
    output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get('World Output')
    if output is None:
        output = sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new('ShaderNodeOutputWorld')
    sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs['Background'], output.inputs['Surface'])
Before returning code, check API arguments, positive dimensions, noncoincident rod endpoints,
explicit transform pivots and fillet radii against the smallest dimension. If execution fails,
use the actual traceback to repair the program. A failed execution without an image supplies
no rendered visual feedback; do not use it to justify unrelated camera or geometry changes.
Preserve explicit failures and unknowns; do not claim verification without a successful render.

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
import math
import random

# Reference inventory (normalized image bounds, estimated from the photograph):
# Architecture: carpet (0,.59)-(1,1), cream back wall (.11,.37)-(.53,.61),
# right wall (.52,0)-(1,.85), bright left partition (0,.32)-(.12,.67).
# Suspended ceiling spans the upper image; a few missing left-edge tiles reveal
# dark cavities and bent grid members. Tile seams converge toward the back.
# Whiteboard: (.59,.26)-(.92,.59), long right-wall rectangle with aluminum frame,
# a central division, and a narrow lower tray. No evidenced writing.
# Flag: (.45,.32)-(.51,.43), hanging beneath an angled pole near the back corner.
# Back-wall fixtures: gray vent (.15,.44)-(.25,.48), open electrical box,
# displaced gray cover, and two small pale labels near (.32,.48).
# Floor debris: dark broken ceiling panels mainly left/center (.02,.64)-(.43,.81),
# narrow metal rails, and overlapping ochre insulation sheets (.56,.67)-(.90,.79).
# Shapes and depths remain approximate; no furniture is visible.
#
# Local profiles, instance placement, and camera parameters are kept separate.
# Approximately 180 SceneAct primitive meshes, including ceiling panels and seams;
# flag uses 13 separately editable stripes plus canton, with no dense microgeometry.

scene = Scene("Damaged classroom")
cream = (.70,.68,.60)
ceiling_color = (.65,.68,.67)
grid_color = (.48,.52,.51)
dark = (.065,.08,.077)
metal = (.48,.53,.54)

def add_box(parent, name, size, center, color):
    obj = box(size=size, center=center, color=color)
    parent.include(name, obj)
    return obj

def place(asset, name, position, rotation=(0,0,0)):
    asset.turn(euler=rotation, pivot=(0,0,0))
    asset.move(position)
    scene.include(name, asset)
    return asset

room = Asset("Room shell")
add_box(room, "Carpet slab", (5.5,12,.12), (-.25,-2,-.06), (.115,.125,.112))
add_box(room, "Rear plaster", (5.6,.15,3.9), (-.25,4.075,1.95), cream)
add_box(room, "Right plaster", (.15,12,3.9), (2.575,-2,1.95), (.76,.735,.66))
add_box(room, "Left wall", (.12,12,3.9), (-3.06,-2,1.95), (.78,.79,.75))
add_box(room, "Rear dark skirting", (5.5,.045,.13), (-.25,3.985,.065), dark)
add_box(room, "Right dark skirting", (.045,12,.14), (2.485,-2,.07), dark)
scene.include("Architecture", room)

# Independent ceiling tile instances; the dark plenum is visible through omissions.
ceiling = Asset("Suspended ceiling")
add_box(ceiling, "Dark plenum above openings", (5.5,12,.07), (-.25,-2,4.09), (.08,.105,.105))
tile_w, tile_d = .61,1.22
for ix in range(9):
    for iy in range(10):
        x = -3 + (ix+.5)*tile_w
        y = -8 + (iy+.5)*tile_d
        missing = ix == 0 and iy in (5,6,7)
        if not missing:
            c = (.66+.012*((ix+iy)%3), .69+.009*((ix+iy)%3), .68)
            add_box(ceiling, "Acoustic tile %02d %02d"%(ix,iy),
                    (tile_w-.013,tile_d-.013,.035),(x,y,3.9),c)
for ix in range(10):
    add_box(ceiling,"Long grid %d"%ix,(.014,12.2,.023),
            (-3+ix*tile_w,-1.9,3.875),grid_color)
for iy in range(11):
    add_box(ceiling,"Cross grid %d"%iy,(5.49,.014,.023),
            (-.255,-8+iy*tile_d,3.875),grid_color)
scene.include("Ceiling grid and panels",ceiling)

# A pair of inset translucent fluorescent panels.
for i,y in enumerate((-1.3,1.14)):
    fixture=Asset("Fluorescent ceiling fixture")
    add_box(fixture,"Metal rim",(.59,1.19,.03),(0,0,0),(.55,.59,.58))
    add_box(fixture,"Clouded diffuser",(.55,1.14,.015),(0,0,-.024),(.78,.82,.81))
    place(fixture,"Ceiling light %d"%i,(-1.78,y,3.866))

# Whiteboard local frame: thin dimension along local X, length along local Y.
board=Asset("Wall whiteboard")
board_length, board_height = 3.45,1.83
add_box(board,"White enamel surface",(.034,board_length,board_height),(0,0,0),(.78,.80,.79))
for y in (-board_length/2,board_length/2):
    add_box(board,"Vertical frame %.2f"%y,(.057,.035,board_height+.06),(-.018,y,0),metal)
for z in (-board_height/2,board_height/2):
    add_box(board,"Horizontal frame %.2f"%z,(.06,board_length+.035,.035),(-.018,0,z),metal)
add_box(board,"Panel joining strip",(.042,.018,board_height),(-.025,.52,0),(.68,.71,.70))
add_box(board,"Marker ledge",(.105,board_length,.035),(-.065,0,-board_height/2-.025),metal)
place(board,"Whiteboard on right wall",(2.455,.97,2.22))

# Bright flat partitions along the left side.
partition=Asset("Left pale partition panels")
for i in range(6):
    add_box(partition,"Panel %d"%i,(.035,1.12,2.85),(0,i*1.13,1.425),(.87,.88,.85))
    add_box(partition,"Vertical joint %d"%i,(.043,.013,2.85),(-.006,i*1.13-.56,1.425),(.70,.73,.72))
place(partition,"Left partitions",(-2.985,-3.25,0))

fixtures=Asset("Back wall fittings")
add_box(fixtures,"Vent dark inset",(.98,.025,.40),(-2.05,3.97,2.15),(.31,.37,.38))
for i in range(7):
    add_box(fixtures,"Vent horizontal louver %d"%i,(.92,.025,.008),
            (-2.05,3.948,1.985+i*.047),(.39,.43,.43))
add_box(fixtures,"Electrical cabinet rim",(.34,.07,.47),(-.72,3.945,1.85),(.48,.52,.50))
add_box(fixtures,"Open cabinet dark interior",(.27,.018,.38),(-.72,3.898,1.85),(.16,.20,.19))
add_box(fixtures,"Cabinet internal plate",(.12,.025,.25),(-.72,3.878,1.86),(.61,.64,.59))
fixtures.include("Exposed cabinet wire",rod(radius=.012,start=(-.80,3.85,1.98),end=(-.77,3.85,1.75),color=(.13,.16,.15)))
cover=box(size=(.52,.045,.43),center=(0,0,0),color=(.40,.46,.44))
cover.turn("y",38,pivot=(0,0,0))
cover.move((-.46,3.84,1.48))
fixtures.include("Hanging tilted cabinet door",cover)
for i in range(2):
    add_box(fixtures,"Wall label %d"%i,(.15,.014,.21),(.04+i*.24,3.973,1.51+i*.04),(.79,.79,.71))
    add_box(fixtures,"Label print %d"%i,(.083,.009,.025),(.04+i*.24,3.961,1.54+i*.04),(.33,.36,.33))
scene.include("Rear wall fixtures",fixtures)

# Flag cloth: editable shallow waviness, with stripes extending down from canton.
flag=Asset("American flag and pole")
flag.include("Angled pole",rod(radius=.012,start=(0,0,0),end=(-.78,-.12,.52),color=(.24,.26,.24)))
# Broad cloth plane follows the hanging flag's narrowing, slightly folded profile.
for i in range(13):
    ztop=.48-i*.079
    width=.43*(.88+.12*math.cos(i*.24))
    stripe=box(size=(width,.014,.081),center=(-.67+width/2,-.13-.025*math.sin(i*.55),ztop-.04),
               color=(.62,.075,.065) if i%2==0 else (.81,.79,.69))
    stripe.turn("y",-7,pivot=(-.67,-.13,.48))
    flag.include("Cloth stripe %02d"%i,stripe)
add_box(flag,"Blue star field",(.195,.018,.43),(-.567,-.16,.267),(.12,.18,.24))
for j in range(4):
    for k in range(3):
        add_box(flag,"Star fleck %d %d"%(j,k),(.012,.005,.012),
                (-.638+k*.054,-.173,.11+j*.085),(.78,.80,.74))
place(flag,"Back corner flag",(1.75,3.83,3.20))

# Fallen acoustic tiles: modest thickness, irregular overlapping orientations.
random.seed(12)
def fallen_panel(name, dimensions, position, angle, color, tilt=(0,0)):
    a=Asset(name)
    add_box(a,"Broken panel body",dimensions,(0,0,dimensions[2]/2),color)
    # A pale torn edge makes the thin slab legible against the carpet.
    add_box(a,"Exposed pale edge",(dimensions[0],.018,.014),
            (0,-dimensions[1]/2,dimensions[2]*.65),(.48,.49,.40))
    return place(a,name,position,(tilt[0],tilt[1],angle))

fallen_panel("Rear fallen tile",(.85,.52,.025),(-1.55,1.65,.015),-12,(.27,.29,.25))
fallen_panel("Rear tile fragment",(.55,.32,.024),(-1.85,1.91,.04),9,(.39,.40,.32))
fallen_panel("Middle left tile",(.95,.54,.025),(-2.12,-.30,.015),-17,(.35,.36,.30))
fallen_panel("Middle tile overlap",(.60,.34,.025),(-1.88,-.12,.045),12,(.24,.26,.23))
fallen_panel("Foreground broad fragment",(1.17,.66,.035),(-1.48,-2.15,.014),14,(.29,.30,.25))
fallen_panel("Foreground upper fragment",(.86,.51,.025),(-1.22,-1.94,.055),-17,(.37,.38,.31))
fallen_panel("Foreground narrow fragment",(.73,.22,.023),(-1.02,-2.24,.078),29,(.22,.25,.22))

insulation=Asset("Fallen yellow insulation sheets")
# Broad thin solids with independently adjustable contour proportions.
add_box(insulation,"Lower ochre slab",(1.29,.94,.055),(0,.10,.045),(.59,.45,.16))
top=add_box(insulation,"Large yellow upper slab",(1.32,1.08,.065),(.27,-.21,.12),(.69,.55,.22))
top.turn("x",-10,pivot=(.27,-.21,.12))
add_box(insulation,"Broken narrow left tongue",(.23,.78,.055),(-.55,-.01,.077),(.67,.53,.20))
place(insulation,"Yellow debris pile",(1.43,-1.49,.012),(0,0,-9))

rails=Asset("Detached metal ceiling rails")
rail_specs=[
    ((-.92,-1.12,.045),(-.05,-1.28,.038)),
    ((-1.85,-.91,.045),(-.92,-1.13,.042)),
    ((1.59,-2.04,.036),(2.48,-3.75,.045)),
    ((1.80,-2.18,.04),(2.50,-4.17,.047)),
    ((2.18,-2.36,.046),(2.50,-3.07,.048)),
]
for i,(p,q) in enumerate(rail_specs):
    dx,dy=q[0]-p[0],q[1]-p[1]
    length=math.hypot(dx,dy)
    a=Asset("Loose T rail")
    add_box(a,"Flat flange",(length,.037,.015),(0,0,.008),(.59,.63,.62))
    add_box(a,"Upright web",(length,.009,.031),(0,0,.025),(.35,.40,.40))
    place(a,"Floor rail %d"%i,((p[0]+q[0])/2,(p[1]+q[1])/2,(p[2]+q[2])/2),
          (0,0,math.degrees(math.atan2(dy,dx))))
scene.include("Small rail scraps",rails)

# A few small light chips, kept sparse at this image resolution.
chips=Asset("Small floor chips")
for i in range(15):
    x=random.uniform(-2.6,2.2)
    y=random.uniform(-3.2,2.9)
    add_box(chips,"Chip %02d"%i,(random.uniform(.025,.075),random.uniform(.025,.09),.007),
            (x,y,.008),(.45,.44,.34))
scene.include("Scattered chips",chips)

# Small ceiling smoke detector.
detector=Asset("Ceiling smoke detector")
d=ball(radius=.09,center=(0,0,0),color=(.73,.74,.68))
d.resize((1,1,.38),pivot=(0,0,0))
detector.include("Detector housing",d)
place(detector,"Smoke detector",(-1.54,-2.35,3.84))

realize(scene)

sc=bpy.context.scene
if sc.world is None:
    sc.world=bpy.data.worlds.new("SceneWorld")
sc.world.use_nodes=True
background=sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("Background")
if background is None:
    background=sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBackground")
output=sc.world.node_tree.nodes.get("World Output")
if output is None:
    output=sc.world.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeOutputWorld")
sc.world.node_tree.links.new(background.outputs["Background"],output.inputs["Surface"])
background.inputs["Color"].default_value=(.71,.76,.79,1)
background.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.35

# Restrained procedural carpet and plaster detail; no photographic textures.
for obj in bpy.data.objects:
    if obj.type != 'MESH':
        continue
    for mat in obj.data.materials:
        if mat is None:
            continue
        mat.use_nodes=True
        bs=mat.node_tree.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        if bs:
            bs.inputs["Roughness"].default_value=.86
    if "Carpet slab" in obj.name and obj.data.materials:
        mat=obj.data.materials[0]
        nt=mat.node_tree
        bs=nt.nodes.get("Principled BSDF")
        noise=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexNoise")
        noise.inputs["Scale"].default_value=165
        noise.inputs["Detail"].default_value=2
        ramp=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeValToRGB")
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].position=.23
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[0].color=(.055,.065,.056,1)
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].position=.78
        ramp.color_ramp.elements[1].color=(.20,.21,.17,1)
        nt.links.new(noise.outputs["Fac"],ramp.inputs[0])
        nt.links.new(ramp.outputs["Color"],bs.inputs["Base Color"])
        bump=nt.nodes.new("ShaderNodeBump")
        bump.inputs["Strength"].default_value=.20
        bump.inputs["Distance"].default_value=.012
        nt.links.new(noise.outputs["Fac"],bump.inputs["Height"])
        nt.links.new(bump.outputs["Normal"],bs.inputs["Normal"])

# Camera estimated independently from rear wall width, corner height, and board edges.
set_view(position=(-2.5,-6,1.65),target=(2.0,4,1.68),lens=26.5,sensor=36)
area_emitter(position=(-2.65,-1.0,2.7),power=560,size=4.5,target=(1,1,1.2),color=(.86,.93,1.0))
area_emitter(position=(-.8,1.1,3.72),power=160,size=2.2,target=(0,0,0),color=(.94,.95,.88))
sc.render.resolution_x=384
sc.render.resolution_y=512
sc.render.resolution_percentage=100
